The headlines
Defense Minister Ashnath Singh says terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to peace

And in Asian para games, the IPG-1G clinches gold in women's 400-metre T20 event.
India Tali reaches 23 medals, including five gold.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, SEO, must
convert the political vision of its leaders into practical cooperation that is visible
in the lives of the people of the region.
Addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Tajikistan today, Mr Singh said,
the organization's 25-year journey provided an opportunity to review its achievements
and discuss its future direction.
The minister emphasized that the three pillars of security, connectivity and opportunity
are mutually reinforcing and essential for achieving tangible benefits for the
India supports initiatives that connect markets, strengthen trade, and create new opportunities
for growth.
The International North-South Transport Corridor and Chabahar Port can play a significant role
in connecting Central Asia with global trade networks.
However, these efforts must be supported by sustained consultations and a comprehensive
framework that includes community engagement, connectivity, and territorial integrity.
Mr. Singh said terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to peace and development of
the region. He said terrorism causes the loss of innocent lives, disrupts investment and
economic capabilities, radicalizes societies, and deprives young people of opportunities.
Mr. Singh asserted that there can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards
in combating it, and no place for those who finance, support, or provide safe havens to
terrorists. He called for collectively dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism.
Terrorism and violence remain among the most serious threats. Terrorism not only causes
loss of human lives, but also adversely affects investment and trade. Therefore,
there can be no justification for terrorism, notable standards in dealing with it,
and no place for those who provide financial or other forms of support. The entire ecosystem
of terrorism must be dismantled and its root causes must be eliminated.
Asia, including the recent attacks on Saudi Arabia, more from our correspondent.
According to the Ministry of External Affairs, the visit of UAE foreign minister will be an
opportunity to review all facets of bilateral cooperation under the India-UAE Comprehensive
Strategic Partnership.
The two sides will assess and take forward initiatives in the area of energy, trade
and investments, fintech, defence and connectivity.
Fartuna Akashwani, Mumbai.
External Affairs Minister Dr S.J. Shankar met the U.S. congressional delegation in Mumbai
today in a social media post. Dr. J. Shankar appreciated their positive sentiments and
interest in taking inter-US ties forward. He said, during the meeting they discussed
trade, energy, security, and technology aspects of our relationship.
The external affairs minister said they also spoke about ease of doing business
in India and deepening Indo-Pacific cooperation between the two countries.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will arrive in Mumbai today for an official visit to India.
Shortly after his arrival, Secretary Rubio will be tribute to victims of terror during a solemn
wreath-laying ceremony at the Taj Memorial. Inside the historic Hotel Taj Mahal Palace,
he will hold bilateral meeting with external Affairs Minister S.J. Shankar in Mumbai this
afternoon, the dialogue is expected to cover key aspects of the India-U.S. strategic partnership,
economic cooperation, regional stability and energy security. Later in the evening, Secretary
Rubio is scheduled to attend the Freedom 250 reception at the Geo-World Convention Center,
celebrating key milestones in U.S. history and bilateral diplomatic ties.
Tomorrow, Secretary Rubio will complete the Mumbai leg of his visit and in plane for
Jamnagar in Gujarat. Union Home Minister Amit Shah met the family members of Vikram
Jeet Singh in Batala, Gurdaspur in Punjab today. Vikram Jeet Singh was allegedly killed by drug
traffickers recently. The Home Minister is on a day-long visit to Punjab to meet the family
members of those who paid with their lives for raising their voice against the drug
menace in the state. More from our correspondent. The Home Minister has now moved to Sangroor
from Gurdaspur. He will be meeting the family members of Gulzar Singh who committed suicide
allegedly when his pleas were not heard by the state government against the sale of drugs
which made his son a drug addict. Sanguru is the home district of Punjab Chief Minister
Bhagwan Singh Mahan. His third visit will be to Mansa where an anti-drug activist Pravinder
Singh Chhota was recently shot dead by a chemist for objecting him to selling synthetic
drugs. The Home Minister will meet his bereaved family members. The body of the activist has
not yet been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. His father has said he will
not cremate his son till the justice is delivered. Chhota's father Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman,
while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case.
Meanwhile, just few hours before the arrival of Home Minister to Punjab, Chief Minister
Bhagman Man announced to hand over the murder case of Pravinder Singh to Central Bureau of
Investigation. Later, Shrisha will participate in Dussehra Ceremony in Luddhiana, where the
burning of Ravana's effigy has symbolically been themed as Ravana of Chitta i.e. drugs.
Rajesh Bali, Akash Vani News, Jalandhar.

During the annual Vijay Dasmi Utsav celebrations of the RSS at Resimbaag ground in Nagpur this
morning, Dr. Bhagwat said forces seeking to dismantle the country are working with planned
strategies. He cautioned that regime change agitations do not resolve fundamental problems,
warning that protests could become instruments of political interest and fuel divisions
in society rather than delivering solutions.
A storm has risen from the west that stand opposed to every form of order, civility and human values.
It seeks to destroy and devastate them.
Even developed countries are bearing the brunt of this storm,
as those who serve the interests of their own selfish agendas continue to wield influence everywhere.
India's rise will help curb such action.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi today extended his greetings to the workers of the Rashtriya
Saibhaka Sangh RSS on its 101st Foundation Day in a social media post.
Mr. Modi said the RSS has completed a remarkable century of service, nation-building and social
harmony.
He said countless workers of the organization have worked for society with a deep sense
of duty and a nation-first spirit.
The Prime Minister wished that this spirit would keep strengthening national development
present in times to come.
The Festival of Vijay, Dashmi and Dashera which marks the triumph of good over evil is
being celebrated across the nation today.
This joyous day marks the culmination of the Nine Day Navratri Festival and the Grand Durga
Puja celebrations.
The ceremonial Ravana Dehan or burning of effigies of Ravana, Kumbhakarna and Meghnaad
also takes place today.
In Karnataka Mahanabhumi, the ninth day of the Navratri festival is celebrated as Ayudhapuja,
when commercial establishments perform puja of their machineries and households offer prayers to the tools used by them in daily life.
More from our correspondent.
Ayudhapuja is celebrated across Karnataka today when the vehicles, factories, offices clean their premises
and offer puja to the machineries and tools used by them.
They are decorated with banana and mango leaves along with traditional flower arrangements.
A white pumpkin is split and kept at the doorway toward of Ivil.
At home, two puja is performed to the books and tools used in daily life.
At Mysoro Palace, Aayu the puja is performed by the Daayan of the royal family,
to the armory, the palanqueens and other emblems.
The 10 days grand Dasara festival will end tomorrow with Vijay Dasmi festival.
In Mysoro, a grand procession called Jambusavari is arranged
with elephants forming an important part of it.
Sudhendra Akashwani News, Bengaluru
The Shera symbolizing the victory of good over evil is being celebrated across Himachal Pradesh today
with traditional enthusiasm and further, the festival also marks the culmination of the nine-day Navratri celebrations.
Chief Minister Sukvinder Singh Sukhu will burn the effigies of Ravan, Kumbhakaran and Meghnath at Jakku Temple in Simlaat this evening for report.
The world-famous 7-day international Kulu Dasheera, renowned for its unique traditions,
will commence tomorrow with the Rath Yatra of Lord Raghunath.
The festival will continue until 27th of this month.
Governor Kavindar Gupta will participate in the Rath Yatra and formally inaugurate
the Kulu Dasheera celebrations this evening at Lalchand Prarthi Kala Kendra.
Arrival of Devuluz, the local deities and their attendants at the Grand Congregation
continues amid the beats of traditional drums and other musical instruments.
Mata Hidimba arrived in Kullu from Manali today, with Ritesh Kapoor's report, Komadiparek,
Akashwani News, Delhi.
India has reiterated its offer to put its commitment to not being the first to use nuclear weapons
and not to use them against non-nuclear weapon states into a multilateral legal agreement.
Addressing the United Nations General Assembly's first committee in New York, Member of Parliament
Manish Devari said, India remains committed to universal, non-discriminatory and verifiable
nuclear disarmament through a multilateral framework.
India remains committed to nuclear disarmament, that is, universal, non-discriminatory and
verifiable.
This goal can be achieved by a step-by-step process underwritten by universal commitment
to an agreed non-discriminatory multilateral framework.
As a responsible nuclear weapons state, India maintains a policy of credible minimum deterrence
with a posture of no first use and non-use against non-nuclear weapons states.
At the Asian Paragames in Aichi Nagoya, Japan, India have won a total of 24 medals so far,
including 5 gold, 8 silver and 11 bronze.
Indian Parathlete Deep Djiwanji clinched gold in the women's 400m T20 event, setting
a new games record with a time of 56.36 seconds, a victory marked India's fifth gold medal
at the competition, we have a report. In the Men's 65kg powerlifting event, India's
Ashok won the silver medal with the best lift of 192 kgs, China's reigning Paralympic
champion Jouvi claimed gold, while Indonesia's Margono secured bronze.
In the Men's 10-metre air pistol SH1 event, Indian parachuter Manish Narwal won silver,
scoring 233.7 points in the final. Earlier, Indian Paratable Tennis players
Devi Sahanaravi and Prachi Pandey won bronze medals in the Women's Singles class 9 and class 6 events.
Bhavina Patel secured a bronze medal in the Women's Singles class 4-5 semifinals.
Sonal Ben Patel also secured a bronze in the Women's Singles class 3 event
after losing her semifinal against South Korea's Yoon Ji-woo in straight games 7-11,
5-11, 6-11. Jigasa Pandey, Akashwani News, Delhi.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh says terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to peace
and development called upon SEO for collective efforts to dismantle entire terror ecosystem.
Union Home Minister Amit Shah meets family members of anti-drug activists in Punjab.
State government decides to hand over murder case of Parvinder Singh Chhotatu, CBI.
The external affairs minister is Jay Shankar to hold talks with his UAE counterpart in Mumbai
to review comprehensive strategic partnership and West Asia crisis.
With that, we end the midday news.
